newsitem.title: HUNGARY: ICE RATES ZWACK AS "BUY" ON BETTER OUTLOOK.
newsitem.headline: ICE RATES ZWACK AS "BUY" ON BETTER OUTLOOK.

text.p: A new analyst report predicted spirits producer Zwack Unicum Rt would achieve higher earnings this year than last despite sluggish domestic market and recommended the share as a "buy".

The report, by ICE Securities of London, said internal cost-controlling organisational measures had contributed to improved prospects for the company, whose flagship product is the bitter-sweet liqueur Unicum.

"Whilst Zwack still operates in a somewhat depressed domestic legal spirits market, the company, with its greatly improved logistic, inventory and financial control, is certain to maintain its market leader status," analyst Rudi Voros said.

Voros foresaw a waning of the negative impact on consumer spending of the government's 1995 austerity measures and detected signs that the government is beginning to tackle illegal alcohol sales, creating an improved market environment.

"As the purchasing power of the domestic consumers is gradually restored during 1997, we foresee a significant improvement in Zwack's profitability which is not reflected by the current share price," Voros said.
"In our opinion the upward share price correction will precede this improvement in profitability and accordingly we recommend purchases."
The report forecasts a modest increase in sales this year followed by a 26 percent jump in 1997 while income growth will outpace inflation in both years.
It also forecast Zwack to boost its net profit to 686 million forints on sales of 13 billion forints in 1996 from figures of 509 million and 12.37 billion, respectively, in 1995.
For 1997 ICE predicted Zwack's net profit to 933 million on sales of 16.4 billion forints.

Voros said the company structure forms a good framework for exports through strategic partners Underberg of Germany, which through a 50-50 Austrian joint venture with Zwack owns 50 percent plus one share of the company, and IDV, part of Grand Metropolitan, which holds a 26 percent stake.

The company is benefitting from the partnership with Underberg through Underberg's experience in the European bitter liqueur market, the ICE report said, while its association with IDV has opened "a window of opportunities."

Zwack generates five percent of its sales through exclusive marketing rights for many IDV products, including Jack Daniels whiskey, while the marketing of Zwack products through IDV channels is also bearing fruit, Voros said.
On the Budapest Stock Exchange Zwack shares ended at 2,850 forints, down 50 in light turnover.
